correctness.rationale: The relative Borel–Moore/symmetric-square compact-pair isomorphism is canonical; pair-homotopy invariance reduces to a rose. The rose has relative boundary ∂u_i=2a_i and ∂z_ij=0, producing exact integral groups. Natural H1 is coker(2V→V), and natural H2 comes from cross-product classes q_*(α×β) forming an integral rectangle basis and from injectivity of the diagonal on H1. All graph-homeomorphism actions commute with those maps; the exterior-square trace follows by elementary linear algebra. Independent finite cellular chain ranks, integral Smith forms and Lefschetz traces passed in the packaged script. No experiment is treated as an all-graph proof.

value.rationale: A complete integral, automorphism-natural classification for every finite connected graph refines the 2026 abstract BM groups into computable torsion and exterior-square symmetry modules. Distinct graph symmetries can have different top BM traces despite identical underlying groups (e.g. swapping two independent cycles acts by -1 on the exterior-square class). It determines all rational top characters from ordinary graph H1, without enumerating a noncompact configuration space. The claim is about full symmetry modules, not a mere rank recitation; it does not claim a new general symmetric-product homology theorem.
